title: Borealis: deterministic throughput proving harness and customer acceptance playbook
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Objective: Build a deterministic, repeatable load-testing harness (codename 'Borealis') and an associated customer acceptance playbook that proves Dedicated capacity throughput guarantees. The harness must produce reproducible throughput/latency signatures across tenants, quantify tail behavior under microbursts, and generate artifacts customers can sign off on. This ticket covers: 1) a benchmarking methodology with statistical confidence targets; 2) the load harness implementation and parametrization; 3) a staged customer acceptance test plan and artifact templates for operational handoff.

Key goals:
- Provide a single canonical procedure to validate SLA commitments (throughput and tail latency) for dedicated pools.
- Ensure reproducibility across runs and clusters with tenant-aware workload mixes and cache-priming recipes.
- Produce a customer-facing evidence bundle (replay script, raw telemetry, synthesized report, Grafana bookmarks, and pass/fail checklist).

Out of scope: full autoscaler implementation changes (this ticket defines experiment variants and run plans only).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Harness can run a 4-stage acceptance scenario (smoke, ramp, stress, soak) end-to-end against a Dedicated pool in our staging fleet.
2) Each run produces a certificate.json with: run id, cluster id, workload profile, seed, steady-state windows, p50/p95/p99 latency, achieved aggregate tokens/sec, cache hit rates, and pod-level CPU/GPU utilization.
3) Statistical confidence: p95 latency measured with 95% bootstrap CI width <= 10% relative. Throttle/variance analysis demonstrates <5% run-to-run throughput variance for steady-state windows >= 5 minutes.
4) Customer acceptance playbook (checklist + artifact templates) reviewed and approved by Solutions Eng and Legal.
5) At least two internal pilots completed (one PLG customer, one enterprise with multi-tenant trace).
runbook_steps:
Stage 0 — Preparation:
- Select target dedicated pool and snapshot current routing policy.
- Ensure model variant pinned for the run; record model checksum.
- Deploy 'borealis-prober' k8s Job with config: tenant-mix.json, token-length-dist.json, microburst-profile.json.

Stage 1 — Smoke:
- Run 1 minute single-tenant sanity probe at 5% target QPS. Verify KV cache warms to expected hit rate (>30% for cached prompt sets).

Stage 2 — Ramp:
- Linear ramp to target QPS over 5 minutes. Observe autoscaler signals but do not alter policies mid-run. Capture pod spin-up latencies.

Stage 3 — Stress (microburst matrix):
- Execute 3 microburst patterns (short-high, medium, long) injected across tenant slices. Measure p99 amplification and tail latency recovery.

Stage 4 — Soak (steady-state verification):
- Maintain target QPS for 20 minutes. Collect steady-state telemetry, token counts, and sample outputs for correctness regressions.

Post-run — Artifact collection:
- Collect traces, aggregated latency histograms, per-pod resource profiles, kernel-level GPU util, and KV cache hit-rate timelines. Generate evidence bundle and run certificate.

Repro tips: pin random seeds, use deterministic traffic generator (borealis-replayer), and run with identical cluster topology and traffic shaping rules.
measurement_metrics:
Primary metrics: aggregate tokens/sec (throughput), request/sec (RPS), p50/p95/p99 latency (ms), tail amplification factor (post-burst p99 / pre-burst p99), KV cache hit ratio, queue depth, pod GPU utilization, OOM/restart count.
Secondary metrics: cost-per-token estimate (using current pricing overlay), scheduling latency distribution, cold-start penalty, and warm-cache delta.
Statistical methodology: run N=5 independent experiments per profile; compute bootstrap 95% CI for each metric. For long soaks, compute moving-window variance and require coefficient of variation <= 0.05 in steady-state windows. Use Kolmogorov-Smirnov to compare latency distributions across runs for regression detection.
autoscaler_experiments:
We will run three autoscaler policy variants during experiments (one policy per run series):
A) Conservative scale: high cpu/gpu thresholds, long cooldown (baseline behavior).
B) Aggressive scale: low thresholds, short cooldown, allow rapid pod addition for microbursts.
C) Predictive buffer: proactive scale-up based on traffic forecast and prefix cache occupancy.
Experiment goals: quantify tradeoffs between tail latency, cost, and overshoot. Measure wasted capacity during bursts and recovery time under each policy. Capture triggering signals (queue depth, token-ps trend, KV cache miss rate) to feed back into policy tuning.
Acceptance criteria per experiment: steady-state throughput achieved with p95 latency within SLA +/- 10%; microburst recovery time within policy target; and cost delta reported in evidence bundle.

notes: Implementation notes: use a mix of synthetic prompts that mimic customer p50 and p95 token lengths; include 'cold-path' prompts (no cache) to exercise kv-cache miss behavior. Ensure load generators respect rate limits and backoff semantics to avoid breaking shared infra. For customer signoff, include a short narrative that explains deviations (if any) and recommended guardrails for routing/fallbacks.
